card.title: The Leak Is Spreading
card.instruction: Interpret every new question or coincidence as evidence that concealed information is escaping faster than it can be contained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The florist asked what time our surprise party starts. How did it get out?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I told her so she'd deliver before Dad arrives.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now the driver knows. Can you collect the flowers yourself?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. I'll ask the baker to give me a lift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It's reached the baker while we were containing the florist. How many stops is this lift making?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 treats the florist's timing question as a leak, A3 infers driver spread and changes collection, and A5 interprets B's lift solution as another escaped disclosure.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's delivery explanation causes A3's collection plan; B4's baker lift causes A5's expanding-stop suspicion.

relationship.evidence: B2 arranged timely flowers and B4 agrees to collect them while proposing available transport.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's helpful transport plan as proof containment is losing ground before it is implemented.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a surprise party and florist inquiry; B2 names Dad as the protected recipient.
